body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\beta,L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)\), such that for all even \(T\ge32\) and \(B\ge1\), \[cF_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le CF_\alpha(T,b).\] The upper inequality is attained by the implementable hard-cap policy \(\pi^\star\), and the lower inequality holds over all \(\Pi_{T,B}\).
body.justification: The matched upper and lower bounds are the theorem-level design certificate: they identify the exact cost of memory and a common deadline.
body.gap: No named comparator simultaneously imposes deterministic capacity, arrival-incidence matching, terminal perfect pairing, and additive causal precision regret over a Hölder class.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a capacity calculator that is minimax-certified rather than tuned only by simulation.

obligation.what_is_open: The all-regime upper inequality and its attaining policy remain unproved because they require a positive resolution of the endpoint-safe coarsening question.
obligation.obstruction: The lower frontier is proved, but the available implementable policy incurs a terminal residual-cell charge that can exceed the claimed harmonic deadline term when capacity is large relative to the horizon.
obligation.attempted: I combined the sharp weighted-suffix lower bound with the pathwise capped-grid construction and tested whether deterministic geometric coarsening alone removes the residual charge. It does not without a new inherited-workload estimate.
obligation.partial_result:
The completed arguments establish the two-sided partial frontier
\[
cF_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le C\inf_{1\le m\le b}\{m^{-\alpha}+m/T\}.
\]
In particular, the bounds match up to fixed constants throughout \(b^{1+\alpha}\le T\), and they already imply \(R_T(B_T)\to0\) if and only if \(B_T\to\infty\).  The all-regime upper bound remains contingent on the endpoint-safe coarsening workload estimate.
